title: Impact exercise to help make your bones stronger
claims: For people who have not had spinal fractures, the Royal Osteoporosis Society advises building up to 50 moderate-impact exercises on most days of the week; the impacts can be jumps, skips, jogs or hops, and one jump counts as one impact.
The 50 impacts can be spread throughout the day.
For people who have had spinal fractures or many broken bones, the Royal Osteoporosis Society advises building up to 20 minutes of low-impact exercise on most days of the week.

Moderate-impact exercise is defined as pushing off from the ground and landing with a medium force, with both feet leaving the ground at the same time in many exercises; examples include jogging, skipping, dancing and playing tennis.

The Royal Osteoporosis Society advises talking to a doctor or physiotherapist before starting exercise if you have had many broken bones or spinal fractures, are recovering from a broken bone, or have questions about your own situation.
Impact exercise may not be suitable if you have other medical conditions, and strength exercise may need to replace it.
